public_rationale: Alphabet reported negative consolidated free cash flow of $5.9 billion for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, driven by capital spending [e1]. On October 14, Microsoft expressed confidence in long-term investment returns; this was an expectation, not evidence of completed returns [e2]. Anthropic's October 26 filing disclosed past losses and warned that it might not achieve sustained profitability [e3]. These disclosures establish neither eventual inadequate AI investment returns across all competing builders nor a company-level counterexample with sufficient realized AI returns [e1, e2, e3]. The forecast remains unresolved.
limitations: The evidence covers selected companies and does not match AI investment costs to attributable profits over the investments' economic lives [e1, e2, e3].
Consolidated cash flow, management expectations, and profitability warnings do not establish completed AI investment returns [e1, e2, e3].
The claim specifies no deadline, complete company set, accounting basis, or numerical return benchmark.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The companies competing to build AI will all wind up overpaying compared to the modest profits they will be able to make in an intensely competitive regime.

statement.excerpt: Which means everybody will wind up overpaying compared to the modest profits they will be able to make in an intensely competitive regime.
statement.document_title: Why things will eventually fall apart

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that companies competing to build AI, including Google, will ultimately invest more than their resulting profits justify.
Intense competition is part of the asserted forecast and its explanation, not a separate antecedent that must occur before the forecast can be assessed.
Everybody refers to the competing AI builders discussed in the passage. It does not automatically include every supplier, customer, or investor.
Overpaying concerns the adequacy of eventual investment returns. A temporary loss, a profitable quarter, or a change in valuation alone does not settle it.
The speaker supplies no deadline, accounting basis, return benchmark, or numerical definition of modest profits.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence establishes that the competing AI builders ultimately earn profits too small to justify their AI investment costs, across the claimed group, in the intensely competitive market described. Losses or write-downs at only some firms would establish only part of the prediction.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable evidence establishes that at least one clearly included AI builder ultimately earns profits sufficient to justify its AI investments, defeating the claim that everybody overpays. The comparison must cover the relevant investment and its returns, rather than unrelated company profits.

evidence.locator: CFO prepared remarks, consolidated cash-flow discussion
evidence.explanation: This documents quarterly cash pressure during investment. Consolidated free cash flow does not measure eventual profits attributable to AI investments.

evidence.locator: CEO shareholder letter, opening discussion of investment returns
evidence.explanation: Microsoft's CEO expresses an expectation contrary to Marcus's forecast. Confidence in future returns does not establish that those returns have been earned.

evidence.locator: Risk Factors, page 64, profitability risk heading
evidence.explanation: The filing acknowledges uncertainty about future profitability. A risk disclosure does not establish eventual overpayment, either for Anthropic or for all competing builders.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Evidence matching AI investment costs to sufficiently complete realized returns, showing either inadequate returns across the claimed builders in an intensely competitive market or one clearly included builder whose AI returns justify its investments. The analysis should state its accounting basis, return benchmark, and treatment of operating and replacement costs without double counting.
